claim: Three reasons to care about presence, being in the moment, "now-ness": we all want them, and being fully present improves all of them
Happiness is one reason to care about presence: more present, you're happier, more at peace, more content, period
The more we get out of the present moment, into the past or the future, the more unhappy we are, typically
Effectiveness is one reason to care about presence: in a workout, at your job, in a hobby, more in the moment means more effective
With your mind on tomorrow, on a month ago or on yesterday's conversation with your wife, instead of in the moment, a creative task at work suffers

Relationships are one reason to care about presence: every single interaction and relationship, with your kids, friends, spouse, girlfriend or the cashier at the grocery store, benefits from you being more fully present
The title of the episode on the shortcut to more presence and now-ness kind of misleads: there is no shortcut
There is no shortcut in life. So often we look for one, to losing the weight, getting healthier, building the business
name: Discipline and intention

claim: We all need a reminder at times: shortcuts are so tempting, and they do not exist, they are a lie
name: Discipline and intention

claim: Jocko Willink, probably originally from his podcast (his work is amazing, and highly suggested): "The shortcut is a lie. The hack doesn't get you there." The easy road "will not take you where you want to be. Stronger, smarter, faster, healthier, better, free." Reaching goals, overcoming obstacles and being the best version of you possible will not happen by itself, by cutting corners or by looking for the easy way: "There is no easy way. There is only hard work, late nights, early mornings, practice, rehearsal, repetition, study, sweat, blood, toil, frustration, and discipline."
name: Discipline and intention

claim: There is no shortcut, and that applies to every aspect of our lives, and certainly to presence
name: Discipline and intention

claim: There are tools for presence, absolutely, but like anything else, presence is a lifelong practice
For presence, do the things that lead to it every day and focus on being present every day
No switch makes you present every moment for the rest of your life

For presence, learn what presence really is: we often don't fully understand it, and even if we do, not really how to get back there, or some of the strategies within our own mind and body to get there

A number of books do a really good job of teaching what presence is; the personal favorite, recommended often and highly, truly life-changing for a lot of people who read it or heard the audiobook: *The Power of Now* by Eckhart Tolle, who has a number of really good books
Cold exposure, a cold shower, an ice bath, any kind, is really powerful for fully bringing you into the moment
In a cold shower you're not thinking about next week's bill, tomorrow's project or a conversation from two days ago: the cold brings you 100% to that moment
One of the most powerful ways to more presence and awareness is habits that bring us to that place: the more often we come back to it, the more often we can return to the now through the day
Cold exposure on a regular basis helps carry presence into moment-to-moment life
Of the so many benefits of daily meditation, one is presence that carries through the rest of your day, especially once it's a daily habit
Daily meditation doesn't have to take forever
A 45-minute meditation that morning, awesome; a lot of days, about 10 minutes
10 minutes a day of meditation will honestly change your life in so many ways, one being more presence

Eyes-closed physical training: close your eyes and move, for the majority or the entire time, with really almost any exercise: certainly bodyweight (push-ups, pull-ups, squats), yoga, kettlebells, resistance bands
name: Exercising with eyes closed

claim: In eyes-closed physical training, when we close our eyes to the outer world, we open them to what's happening inside, in mind, spirit and body, which brings us back into the present moment in a really powerful way
name: Exercising with eyes closed

claim: Eyes-closed physical training has lots of other benefits, covered before and more to come
name: Exercising with eyes closed

claim: Fasting, especially a longer fast: two or three days or longer is really incredible for bringing you to a connected, tapped-in, present place, tapped into the universe and the energy flowing through you
Day three of a water fast is typically when people really experience mental clarity, groundedness and presence
Daily practices bring us back to presence; occasional ones, like a longer fast, bring us there really powerfully, and having accessed that place makes it easier to come back to

Fasting bringing you to presence seems to apply to intermittent fasting too: eating has a big impact on mind and emotions, and cutting back your daily eating window has so many benefits, probably including more presence. Not as powerful as a three-day fast, but it certainly helps

Of the so many things you can do for presence, another is simply intention: especially once you've learned and experienced full presence, just paying attention to whether you're really present is a huge part of it, maybe the biggest
Realizing you're lost in the future or the past takes presence: in that moment, you are present
For presence, pay attention day to day and come back
No matter how adept you get, you're always going to get pulled out of presence

Until we learn about presence and practice it, the majority of us are truly fully present very, very little, maybe 1% of the time, literally probably 99% of the time or more not really fully present, caught up in our head
We all get brief glimpses of presence: some sport, a hobby that brings a flow state, sex
Rock climbing has always brought brief glimpses of presence

With practice (reading *The Power of Now*, knowing how presence feels and how to come back, meditating every day), you gradually up the percentage of time you're fully present, to 10%, 20%, 30%, maybe eventually 60, 70, 80, 90% of the time, something like that, but never 100%: it's just not the way it works
Presence is like being on the path of discipline, improving and executing everything every single day: we're never on it 100% of the time, we always fall off, and what matters is getting back on
With presence, it's always up to you to notice you got swept up in thoughts and come back
Presence also means better sex: one of the very, very best things you can do for sex is to learn, practice and be fully present

You've probably had sex caught up in worry about performing or lasting, in work stress or in a conversation with your partner two days ago, all of which gets in the way big time of an enjoyable, connected, powerful experience

There are other ways to be present, but these are some of the best and most powerful, suggested for use: meditate, use cold exposure, learn about presence and read *The Power of Now*, use eyes-closed exercise
You may find other ways to be present that work for you
For presence, get into your body and your physical surroundings, touched on in *The Power of Now* and an occasional reminder here
Not present means lost in your head, in thoughts of the past and the future; body and surroundings are two really good ways back to presence
To get into your body for presence, close your eyes and move, or don't even close them, just pay attention to your body
For presence, in the car as you drive, right now: feel the weight of your body on the seat, your feet on the ground, your arms on the door or the console, your hands on the steering wheel
Attention to your physical senses brings your awareness out of your head, the past and the future
To get into your surroundings for presence, really look around
So often we move about only sort of semi-aware of what's actually around us, because a lot of our awareness is lost in thoughts
For presence, touch the things around you, look at them, really pay attention to what's physically in front of and around you right now
Anything worth getting has no shortcut, just the discipline of taking the steps, one foot in front of the other, and presence is the same
name: Discipline and intention

claim: Put some of the ways to presence into practice, remember how beneficial presence is, and don't underestimate the power of fully being in the now
For years and years, hearing people or reading every now and then about being present always just lived as "that sounds good"

When you really dive into presence and bring it into your life in a powerful way, it is incredible, the difference it makes in your world: your inner world, how you feel, your body and health, your relationships, your effectiveness
